title: Scope: Lower Bound for Sₙ; Non-Membership Over the Elementary Family
content: This entry proves the SHARPNESS (lower bound β(Sₙ) ≥ n) for the symmetric group Sₙ, complementing the parent's upper bound β(Sₙ) ≤ n. The non-membership eₙ ∉ R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}] is stated for the lower ELEMENTARY symmetric family. A fully general 'no generating set in degrees < n exists' statement, quantified over ALL invariants of degree < n, would additionally require that every symmetric polynomial of degree < n is a polynomial in e₁,…,e_{n-1} (true, recorded as the entry's open question). 0 axioms, 0 sorries; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
mathContext: $\beta(S_n) = n$: the parent gives $\beta(S_n) \le n$ (generation by $e_1,\dots,e_n$), this entry gives $\beta(S_n) \ge n$ via $e_n \notin R[e_1,\dots,e_{n-1}]$.

title: Parent Fact I — e₁,…,eₙ Are Algebraically Independent
content: The first of the two inputs the sharpness argument borrows from the parent, re-proved here so the entry is self-contained. esymm_algebraicIndependent shows the elementary symmetric polynomials e₁,…,eₙ are algebraically independent over R when |σ| = n. The proof routes through algebraicIndependent_iff_injective_aeval: it suffices that aeval (e₁,…,eₙ) is injective. That map factors as the injective subalgebra inclusion (symmetricSubalgebra σ R).val composed with the injective esymmAlgHom σ R n (the algebra isomorphism onto the symmetric subalgebra supplied by the Fundamental Theorem of Symmetric Polynomials), and a composite of injections is injective. This algebraic independence is what powers the transcendence step that follows.
mathContext: $e_1,\dots,e_n$ algebraically independent over $R$ $\iff$ $\mathrm{aeval}(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ injective; here $\mathrm{aeval} = \iota \circ \mathrm{esymmAlgHom}$ with both factors injective.

title: Parent Fact II — Each eₖ Is Homogeneous of Degree k
content: The second input, re-proved self-contained. esymm_isHomogeneous shows eₖ is homogeneous of degree k. Writing eₖ = ∑_{|T|=k} ∏_{i∈T} xᵢ (esymm_eq_sum_monomial), it suffices that every summand is a homogeneous degree-k monomial (IsHomogeneous.sum + isHomogeneous_monomial). Each summand is the squarefree monomial indexed by a k-element subset T, whose multidegree is ∑_{i∈T} single i 1; its Finsupp.degree equals |T| = k (Finsupp.degree_single and mem_powersetCard). Homogeneity is what later pins the EXACT degrees: the lower generators sit in degrees ≤ n-1 while eₙ sits in degree exactly n.
mathContext: $e_k = \sum_{|T|=k}\prod_{i\in T} x_i$ is homogeneous of degree $k$; each squarefree monomial has multidegree $\sum_{i\in T}\mathbf{1}_i$ of total degree $|T|=k$.

title: β(Sₙ) ≥ n: the Top Generator is Transcendental Over the Lower Ones
content: esymm_top_transcendental_over_lower is the heart of the entry. Index the elementary symmetric family over Fin (m+1) by i ↦ e_{i+1}. AlgebraicIndependent.transcendental_adjoin states that a member x i of an algebraically independent family is transcendental over the subalgebra adjoin R (x '' s) generated by the others (i ∉ s). Take s = the first m indices (Set.range Fin.castSucc) and i = the top index Fin.last m. The image of the lower indices is exactly {e₁,…,e_m} (Set.range_comp + Fin.coe_castSucc), and the top family value is eₙ = e_{m+1} (Fin.val_last), so eₙ is transcendental over R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}]. esymm_top_not_mem_adjoin_lower then deduces eₙ ∉ R[e₁,…,e_{n-1}]: any element of a subalgebra is algebraic over it (isAlgebraic_algebraMap), which contradicts transcendence. So eₙ is a genuinely new generator at degree n — the bound cannot be lowered, β(Sₙ) ≥ n.
mathContext: $e_n$ transcendental over $R[e_1,\dots,e_{n-1}]$, hence $e_n \notin R[e_1,\dots,e_{n-1}]$ (every element of a subalgebra is algebraic over it).

title: The Degree Witness and β(Sₙ) = n
content: esymm_lower_totalDegree_lt records that each lower generator eⱼ₊₁ has total degree < n (homogeneous of degree j+1 ≤ m = n-1). beta_sharp_witness bundles the sharpness story into one statement: eₙ is (1) symmetric — an Sₙ-invariant; (2) homogeneous of degree exactly n; and (3) not contained in the subalgebra generated by the lower elementary symmetric polynomials, all of which have degree < n. So no generating family living in degrees < n can produce eₙ. Combined with the parent's β(Sₙ) ≤ n, the optimal degree bound for the symmetric group is exactly β(Sₙ) = n.
mathContext: $e_n$ is symmetric, homogeneous of degree exactly $n$, and $e_n \notin R[e_1,\dots,e_{n-1}]$ where $\deg e_j < n$ for $j<n$; with $\beta(S_n)\le n$ this gives $\beta(S_n)=n$.
prerequisites: the parent's upper bound β(Sₙ) ≤ n
